user_goal: Provide one understandable revision in durable progress/resume receipts without making the user interpret manifest_version, controller revision, protocol version or Git SHA.

accepted_model.name: Human Durable Revision
accepted_model.date_semantics: calendar context from the authoritative persisted timestamp exactly as encoded
accepted_model.ordering_semantics: rN orders revisions only within the same revision scope
accepted_model.sequence_source: existing authoritative monotonic durable task/owner version

why_not_svn_clone: SVN's repository-wide natural-number revision is useful because SVN has a centralized repository commit stream. The current system uses separate Git repositories and durable owner/task streams. Emulating one shared SVN counter would create a new mutable authority, locking/coordination, timezone/reset policy, failure recovery and cross-repository contention.
why_not_daily_counter: RYYYYMMDD.001 would need a new counter and reset boundary; it could race, drift or duplicate. The accepted design reuses an existing monotonic sequence instead.

scope_and_adoption.future_owner_rule: Map only to an already-existing monotonic durable version whose identity lifetime matches the intended revision scope, plus a stable scope code. If none exists, omit the human revision and fix owner versioning separately; never invent a display-only counter.
scope_and_adoption.gap_meaning: Internal safe checkpoints, lease/control metadata or other durable transitions may consume r values; gaps are not missing releases and are never backfilled.

complexity_and_bloat_review.runtime_cost: O(1) formatting from metadata already loaded for the receipt
